newsitem.title: USA: Intel sees Q3 revenues up from Q2.
newsitem.headline: Intel sees Q3 revenues up from Q2.

text.p: Intel Corp said it expects its third quarter revenues to be better than previously forecast.
The world's largest semiconductor maker now is forecasting third quarter sales will be up five percent or more from its second quarter revenue of $4.62 billion.
Intel also said its "turns" or orders from customers seeking immediate delivery, appear to be better than originally expected. The company said it will report third quarter earnings on October 14.

Intel, widely regarded as a bellwether for the technology industry, previously forecast third quarter revenues would be flat with the second quarter and gross margins would be at the upper end of the model of 50 percent, plus or minus a couple of points.
On Monday, the company said in a statement that it now expects gross margin in the third quarter to be "above the 50 percent plus or minus a couple of points."

In last year's third quarter, Intel reported profits of $931 million, or $1.05 per share, on sales of $4.17 billion. The quarter included a gain of $37 million before taxes, or $0.03 per share after taxes.
The consensus among analysts is for earnings in this year's third quarter of $1.14 per share, according to First Call.
